newsitem.title: FRANCE: GOLF-GOOSEN LEADS FROM THE FRONT.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-GOOSEN LEADS FROM THE FRONT.

text.p: South African Retief Goosen, who led from start to finish, could even afford a double bogey at the final hole as he captured the French Open title on Sunday.
Despite going into the lake at the last, he won his second European Tour title by three strokes and said he was inspired by compatriot Ernie Els's victory in the U.S. Open two weeks ago.
The 28-year-old South African was never headed after his second shot of Thursday's first round found the hole for an eagle two before all the rain interruptions forced a two-round final day.
His two closing rounds of two-under-par 70 gave him a 17-under total of 271 for the National golf course, three better that England's Jamie Spence.

Spence's compatriot Martin Gates crashed from second place at the death. He had pushed playing-partner Goosen hardest, moving to within just one stroke as late as the 15th tee, but dropped five shots over the last four holes.
Gates had to settle for a share of third spot a further stroke back with fellow Britons Raymond Russell, Van Phillips and Darren Clarke.
Goosen, who won last year's Slaley Hall Challenge in England, faltered briefly over his first nine holes of the third round but after four successive birdies from the turn, he kept everyone at bay.
"I never thought I could make double on the last and still win," said Goosen, third here last year.

"Martin made a lot of birdies to nearly catch me and the 15th isn't my favourite hole because I lost the tournament on it last year. But he took the pressure off me there. I just wasn't focused at the last."

About the inspiration of close friend Els, Goosen said: "Seeing Ernie win his second major was great encouragement to me, and I hope I'll be seeing him out in America now because I think this gets me in the Sarazen World Championship."
Goosen's chief threat earlier in the week, U.S. Open runner-up Colin Montgomerie, slipped to a third round 73.
"I made a lot of bad putts in the third round and didn't play very well in between them," said Montgomerie, the world number three who finished seven shots behind Goosen after a closing 69.
